correctness.rationale: The explicit feasible star has a positive eigenpair with eigenvalue Lambda. Fixed symmetric row sums imply the exact Rayleigh difference as a positive sum of within-peripheral diagonal/off-diagonal entries weighted by (Lambda-L_i). The strict inequalities Lambda>L_i follow from m>=2, L_i>0, Lambda^2=h Lambda+Q and Q> L_i^2. Rayleigh-Ritz gives the quantitative global bound and unique equality case; the threshold follows from the positive quadratic root. A standalone symbolic-exact rational verifier checks 495 instances but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The source arXiv:2602.23885v2 gives a nonsharp general reciprocal lower bound, an explicit two-type solution and an SDP construction for arbitrary type counts; it does not supply the exact heterogeneous multi-leaf formula, unique star minimizer and strict stability margin of this theorem. General matrix eigenvalue range literature omits the symmetry constraint. All close-source comparisons remain confined to the stated all-size dominant-row subfamily.

value.rationale: The sharp lower epidemic reproduction number under reciprocal mixing with only marginal contact totals is a stated model uncertainty problem. The theorem explicitly solves an arbitrarily high-dimensional dominant-contact regime, admits heterogeneous leaf totals, proves uniqueness, measures the spectral cost of any within-peripheral contacts and characterizes exact reachability of the subcritical threshold. This is a natural structural classification and an actionable mathematical limit, not an arbitrary finite table or parameter substitution.
